title: Slow-cooker three-bean chilli
subtitle: A deep, hearty vegan chilli that holds well for days
excerpt: Kidney beans, black beans, and pinto beans in a smoky tomato and spice base. Completely plant-based, very filling, and better the next day.
sourceNotes: Three-bean chilli is a widely made American vegan and vegetarian dish, drawing on the tradition of chili con carne minus the meat. No single canonical source; adapted from standard American home-cooking repertoire.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob. The beans hold up very well to freezing.
recipe.batchNotes: Excellent batch-cook recipe. Doubles well and provides multiple meals from one cook.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes significantly better the next day. Make a large batch and refrigerate for up to 5 days.

content.text: Three types of beans, a tin of tomatoes, and a well-seasoned spice base: this is a chilli that relies on variety and depth rather than meat for its body. The kidney beans hold their shape, the black beans add earthiness, and the pinto beans break down slightly into the sauce, thickening it.

Everything goes into the pot raw. There is no browning step needed here because the beans, spices, and tomatoes do all the work over a long slow cook. By the time it is done, the sauce will be thick and dark and deeply flavoured.
Serve with rice or baked potatoes. Good toppings: soured cream, grated cheese, fresh coriander, sliced spring onion.

Add all the beans, {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, {{onion}} diced onions, {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, and {{pepper-red}} diced red pepper to the slow cooker. Add all the spices: {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika, {{chilli-powder}} of chilli powder, and {{coriander-ground}} of coriander. Pour in {{stock-vegetable}} of vegetable stock. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt.
Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 7 to 8 hours, or HIGH for 4 to 5 hours. Stir once or twice during cooking if possible. The sauce will thicken as the pinto beans soften and break down.
Squeeze in {{lime}} lime juice and stir through. Taste and adjust the seasoning, adding more chilli powder if you want more heat. Serve immediately or let it sit for 10 minutes to settle further.

rows.cause: The tinned tomatoes released more liquid than the beans could absorb.
rows.fix: Remove the lid and set to HIGH for 30 to 45 minutes. Or mash some of the pinto beans against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce.

rows.symptom: The beans are still firm after 8 hours
rows.cause: If the beans were very old (from a tin near its end date), or if the slow cooker does not maintain a high enough temperature on LOW, beans can take longer.
rows.fix: Switch to HIGH for a further hour. Alternatively, rinse and use a different tin of beans next time.

rows.symptom: The flavour is flat despite all the spices
rows.cause: Ground spices added without any cooking can taste raw and muted after a long slow cook.
rows.fix: Add an extra teaspoon of smoked paprika and cumin at the end, and squeeze in more lime juice. Next time, fry the spices for 1 minute in oil in a pan before adding to the slow cooker.

rows.symptom: The chilli is too thick to serve
rows.cause: The pinto beans broke down completely and absorbed most of the liquid.
rows.fix: Stir in 100 ml of boiling water and re-season. A chilli this thick is also excellent served as a filling for wraps.

content.text: Bean chilli is an everyday staple in American home cooking. It has settled into British kitchens as a cheap, filling, and meat-free dinner option. The three-bean version gives more variety and texture than a single-bean chilli. It is also one of the best things to batch-cook on a Sunday.
